title: Evaluating Additive Release with a Dynamic Leaching Method for Microplastic Assessment
author: Bridson, Abbel, et al.
materials: Non-specific analyses were performed without any eluate preparation steps. Conductivity was measured using a Thermo Scientific Eutech COND 6+ conductivity metre and pH was measured using a Denver Instruments UB-10 metre. Non-purgeable organic carbon (NPOC) was determined using a GE Sievers InnovOx laboratory TOC analyser with GE autosampler using sodium persulfate and perchloric acid reagents. Eluates were analysed with 15% oxidiser, 1% acid, sparge time of 0.8 min, single sample flush, and blank correction with three replicate measurements per eluate. Calibration was performed using a freshly prepared potassium hydrogen phthalate standard.

steps.title: Prepare microplastic test pieces
steps.instruction: Compound the listed polymer resins with the additives at the w/w percentages shown in Table 1, compression‑mould into 1.2 mm thick sheets, cut the sheets by hand into 2 × 2 mm pieces with shears, wrap the pieces in aluminium foil and store them at room temperature in the dark until use.

steps.title: Weigh microplastic into bottles
steps.instruction: Accurately weigh 500 mg of each microplastic sample (or 25 mg for PVC_DBP) into a 50 mL amber borosilicate glass bottle; prepare three replicate bottles for each sample.

steps.title: Add leaching water
steps.instruction: Add 50 mL of UP water to each bottle, adding to the bottles consecutively with a 2 min interval between bottles, then close each bottle with a PTFE‑lined cap.

steps.title: Incubate leaching bottles
steps.instruction: Place the bottles vertically in a Lab Companion IST‑4075 incubated shaker set to 30 °C, orbital shaking at 120 rpm, and keep the shaker in the dark for up to 64 days.

steps.title: Perform scheduled sampling
steps.instruction: At each time point listed in Table 2, remove the corresponding bottle from the incubator and process the eluate as described.

substeps.instruction: Start – 0 h (no sampling).
Week 1 Monday 9 am – 16 h from test start.
Week 1 Monday 3 pm – 6 h after previous sampling.
Week 1 Tuesday 9 am – 21 d 18 h from test start.
Week 1 Wednesday 3 pm – 1.25 d after previous sampling.
Week 1 Friday 9 am – 1.75 d after previous sampling.
Week 2 Wednesday 9 am – 5 d after previous sampling.
Week 3 Wednesday 9 am – 7 d after previous sampling.
Week 6 Tuesday 9 am – 20 d after previous sampling.
Week 10 Tuesday 9 am – 28 d after previous sampling.
For each sampling point:
a) Decant the entire water phase through a 100‑mesh stainless‑steel wire filter cloth (folded to sit inside a glass funnel) into a 60 mL amber glass vial.
b) Using forceps, carefully retrieve any plastic pieces caught on the filter cloth and return them to the original bottle.
c) Add 50 mL of fresh UP water to the bottle, reseal with the PTFE‑lined cap, and return the bottle to the incubator.
d) Seal the 60 mL amber vial with a PTFE‑lined cap and store it in the dark at 4 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Pre‑concentrate and dry eluates
steps.instruction: Transfer 0.1 – 15 mL of each collected eluate into either a 2 mL high‑recovery micro‑V vial (Agilent) or a 15 mL glass digestion tube, add 10 µL or 100 µL of the appropriate internal standard, and evaporate to dryness.

substeps.instruction: If using a 2 mL micro‑V vial, evaporate with a SP Genevac EZ‑2 Plus centrifugal evaporator at 30 °C under a nitrogen purge (aqueous program with automatic end detection).
If using a 15 mL digestion tube (PVC_DBP samples), evaporate with a blow‑down apparatus at 30 °C under a nitrogen purge.
For eluates in 15 mL tubes, transfer the dried residue to a micro‑V vial by adding three 400 µL aliquots of acetone + 0.1 % formic acid, evaporating each aliquot to dryness as above.

steps.title: Re‑dissolve dried residues
steps.instruction: Re‑dissolve the dried residue in 100 µL methanol (for most samples) or in 1000 µL 1:1 methanol/water (for PA6_HAS and PVC_DBP samples) and analyse the solution within 24 h.

steps.title: Prepare LC‑MS calibration standards
steps.instruction: Prepare a stock calibration standard containing all target analytes at 1 mg mL⁻¹ in acetone; dilute this stock to produce working standards ranging from 0.1 ng mL⁻¹ to 1000 ng mL⁻¹ in methanol. Prepare an internal verification standard in the same way and an internal‑standard mixture at ≈10 µg mL⁻¹, adding 10 ng mL⁻¹ of this mixture to each sample and standard before injection.

steps.title: Run UHPLC‑QTOF‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Analyse the re‑dissolved eluates on an Agilent 1290 Infinity II UHPLC coupled to a 6545 AdvanceBio Q‑TOF MS with Jet Stream ESI source using the conditions below.

substeps.instruction: Column: Agilent Zorbax RRHD Eclipse Plus C18, 2.1 × 50 mm, 1.8 µm; guard column 2.1 × 5 mm.
Mobile phase A: 10 % methanol in water + 0.1 % formic acid; Mobile phase B: methanol + 0.1 % formic acid.
Flow rate: 0.4 mL min⁻¹; column temperature: 40 °C.
Gradient: 5 % B hold 1 min; linear increase to 100 % B from 1 min to 3 min; hold at 100 % B until 8 min total run time.
Injection volume: 5 µL.
Source settings: desolvation gas 300 °C at 12 L min⁻¹, nebuliser pressure 35 psi, sheath gas 275 °C at 12 L min⁻¹.
MS settings: capillary voltage 4000 V, nozzle voltage 500 V, fragmentor voltage 150 V.
Calibration/tuning: direct infusion of Agilent ESI‑L low‑concentration tuning mix.
Acquisition: mass range 100–3000 m/z, high‑sensitivity extended dynamic range, resolution 30 000 FWHM at m/z 450.
Data processing: Agilent MassHunter Quantitative 10.0; confirm target compounds within ±10 ppm mass error, ±0.5 min retention time, and correct carbon‑isotope ratio.

steps.title: Measure conductivity, pH and NPOC
steps.instruction: Perform non‑specific analyses on the original eluates without further preparation.

substeps.instruction: Conductivity: use Thermo Scientific Eutech COND 6+ conductivity meter.
pH: use Denver Instruments UB‑10 meter.

NPOC: use GE Sievers InnovOx laboratory TOC analyser with autosampler; add sodium persulfate and perchloric acid reagents, set oxidiser to 15 %, acid to 1 %, sparge time 0.8 min, single‑sample flush, apply blank correction; run three replicate measurements per eluate; calibrate with a freshly prepared potassium hydrogen phthalate standard.

steps.title: Validate leaching method (solid‑to‑liquid ratios)
steps.instruction: Assess recovery and reproducibility of the DyLeMMA using the polymer/additive combinations and solid‑to‑liquid ratios described.

substeps.instruction: For LDPE_AO, PET_UV and PA6_HAS, test 250 mg (low), 500 mg (mid) and 1000 mg (high) of plastic per 50 mL UP water.
For PVC_DBP, test 10 mg (low), 25 mg (mid) and 250 mg (high) per 50 mL UP water.
After the leaching period, recover the microplastic pieces, dry them at 40 °C under vacuum for 72 h, weigh them and calculate mass‑balance recovery.
Solvent extraction of recovered plastic:
a) Accurately weigh 100 mg of PA6_HAS or 10 mg of PVC_DBP into an extraction tube.
b) Add 4 mL methanol (PA6_HAS) or 4 mL diethyl ether (PVC_DBP).
c) Sonicate with a Bandelin SONOREX sonicator for 30 min.
d) Repeat steps b–c two more times with fresh solvent (total three extractions).
e) Combine all extracts, transfer to a volumetric flask and make up to volume with the same extraction solvent.
f) Analyse the combined extract by the UHPLC‑QTOF‑MS method above.
Perform each leaching condition in triplicate (n = 3) to assess reproducibility.

steps.title: Validate LC‑MS quantitative performance
steps.instruction: Confirm specificity, LOD, LOQ, linearity, accuracy and precision of the LC‑MS method according to Eurachem guidelines.

substeps.instruction: Specificity: inject five replicate UP‑water blanks, diluent blanks and zero‑calibration blanks and compare chromatograms with matrix‑spiked samples.
LOD/LOQ: calculate LOD = 3 × SD and LOQ = 10 × SD from ten replicate injections near the lowest detectable concentration for each analyte.

Linearity: prepare 13 calibration levels spanning 0.1–1000 ng mL⁻¹, inject each level in triplicate, test homoscedasticity with an F‑test (α = 0.05), apply 1/x weighting, and require R² ≥ 0.995 and %RA ≥ 90 %.

Accuracy & precision: spike leaching media at concentrations relevant for each analyte (0.05, 0.5, 5 ng mL⁻¹ for AO‑1076, AO‑1010, AO‑168, UV‑234; 50 and 500 ng mL⁻¹ for HAS‑1 and DBP), run ten replicates per level, and evaluate %RSD (≤6 % for HAS‑1/DBP, ≤4 % for the hydrophobic additives at the highest spike).

steps.title: Validate NPOC measurement
steps.instruction: Assess specificity, LOD, LOQ, linearity, range, accuracy and precision of the NPOC method.

substeps.instruction: Specificity: analyse UP water as a blank.

LOD/LOQ: calculate from ten replicate analyses of near‑zero potassium hydrogen phthalate solutions using the formula so′ = so / √(n + 1 / nb) where so is the estimated SD, n the number of replicates and nb the number of blanks.
Linearity and range: prepare five calibration levels from 0 to 100 ppm NPOC and verify linear response.
Accuracy & precision: spike UP water with 25 ppm potassium hydrogen phthalate, analyse ten replicates and calculate recovery and %RSD.
Improve LOD by baking autosampler vials at 450 °C before use.

description: Validation of the DyLeMMA was performed using different polymer resins, plastic additives, and plastic (solid) to water (liquid) ratios, with recovery and reproducibility also assessed. Four different plastic formulations were evaluated covering four polymers (LDPE, PA6, PET, and PVC) and six additives (AO-1076, AO-1010, AO-168, UV-234, HAS-1 and DBP). For each plastic, the method was evaluated at three different solid to liquid ratios. For LDPE_AO, PET_UV, and PA6_HAS solid to liquid ratios of 250 mg (low), 500 mg (mid), and 1000 mg (high) per 50 mL were evaluated. For PVC_DBP solid to liquid ratios of 10 mg (low), 25 mg (mid), and 250 mg (high) per 50 mL were evaluated. Recovery was determined by mass balance, with microplastic samples recovered at the conclusion of the leaching experiment, dried (40 °C under vacuum for 72 h), weighed, and solvent extracted. Solvent extraction was performed by accurately weighing 100 mg of PA6_HAS or 10 mg of PVD_DBP into an extraction tube, adding 4 mL of solvent (methanol for PA6_HAS and diethyl ether for PVC_DBP), and sonicating (Bandelin SONOREX) for 30 min. The extraction process was repeated three times with fresh solvent. The extracts were combined in a volumetric flask, made to volume with extraction solvent, and analysed by LC-MS. Reproducibility of the DyLeMMA was assessed using replicate leaching treatments (n = 3). The LC-MS and NPOC methods were validated according to Eurachem guidelines [19] with respect to specificity, limit of detection (LOD), limit of quantification (LOQ), linearity, range, accuracy, and precision (repeatability) (Table 4). For the LC-MS method, specificity was evaluated comparing chromatograms of five replicate matrix (UP water) blanks, diluent blanks, and zero calibration blanks with matrix spikes.
